_provenance: logs/*/games/*.json frozen at 2026-08-19T23:26:26; 696 completed persuasion games (343 buyer-seat, 353 seller-seat); extractor scratchpad/pers/{pl.py,rows.py}
estimand: P(quality_t = high | seller message_t, seller's message history, qualities revealed so far, round, config)
identification: Quality is revealed only on rounds the buyer bought. The buy decision is a function of observables only, so quality_t is independent of bought_t given the buyer's full decision state; estimating on bought rounds is unbiased WITHIN cells the buyer's policy actually visits.

Positivity does not hold everywhere: states the champion buyer never buys in are never observed. The `randomized` probe's buyer buys with a KNOWN probability clamp((p*v/price - 0.4)/1.2, 0, 1) that ignores the message and the history, so its 61 buyer games give a selection-free sample used for validation and for off-policy evaluation.

model.name: discrete type filter over the seller's lie rate q = P(recommend | low quality)
model.prior_fit: nonparametric MLE (EM) over the q grid, fit on the full message+reveal sequences of all 343 buyer-seat games
model.prior_shape: strongly BIMODAL: 41.1% of mass at q<=0.075 (honest sellers), 40.7% at q>=0.95 (always-recommend shills), 11.2% between 0.3 and 0.5. A Beta prior is the wrong family; the bimodality is what makes one negative message near-decisive at low p.
model.eps_measured: 1 of 2,141 revealed high-quality rounds carried a negative message (text 1/1166, binary 0/975). Field sellers essentially never decline a sale on a good unit, which is what makes the single-parameter q identification work.
model.update: w_j <- w_j * likelihood_j after EVERY round, whether or not the buyer bought; renormalise

predictive.qbar: sum_j w_j * q_j  (posterior mean, computed BEFORE this round's update)

model.unparsed_messages: treated as positive (they behave like positives: P(high|unparsed, text) = 0.64 vs P(high|positive, text) = 0.76); 255 of 6860 buyer rounds
model.decision_rule: buy iff p_high*v + (1-p_high)*u >= product_price; u is 0 in every observed config

cross_validation.scheme: grouped 5-fold by game_id, prior refit inside each fold

selection_free_holdout.design: prior fit on the 282 policy-probe buyer games; evaluated on the 61 randomized-probe buyer games, where quality reveal is an exogenous coin flip independent of message and history. No leakage and no selection bias.
selection_free_holdout.status: this is the strongest single piece of evidence in the artefact

by_message_mode_in_sample.note: the gain holds in binary mode, where no text classifier is involved at all, so it does not depend on glee_agent.text

decision_value.unit: payoff per round in units of product_price

ipw_on_randomized_buyer_games.note: assumption-light: the randomized probe's reveal probability is known and independent of message and history. It is a per-round (one-step-deviation) value at histories the randomized policy generated; it is biased TOWARD M1, which under its own policy would not receive those free reveals.

direct_method_all_games.warning: MODEL DEPENDENT and self-serving: M2 is both the policy and the outcome model, and 1304 of 6860 rounds flip from no-buy to buy into states never observed. Use the IPW number.

action_change.summary: M2 buys on 4227 of 6860 rounds vs M1's 2988: the current agent is systematically too pessimistic at the start of a game, because it sets p_high = p until it has paid for a purchase.

free_information.claim: the message stream identifies the seller type with ZERO purchases
free_information.note: the advantage is concentrated at low p, exactly the configs where the buy decision is close

sizing.metric: config-matched field-proxy percentile, kernel-smoothed CDF (kernel = one round)
sizing.warning: the proxy over-reads: family proxy 0.507 vs live earned 0.449, a 5.8-point optimism. Treat the family point estimate as an upper bound of about +6.5 and the honest range as +1 to +9.
